clue.text: Greedily grab a lot, holding a celebration in Scotland

parts.note: to hog is to take more than your share

indicators.note: holding means the word for a lot wraps around the little word a

parts.note: a lot of something is many
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grabs greedily at a party in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogmanay is the Scottish New Year's Eve, famous for its street parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogmanay is the Scottish name for the New Year's Eve festivities, a famous Scottish party night.

clue.text: Quick appraisal of county opener in single period of cricket

indicators.note: in places the county's first letter inside the word for single

parts.note: single means one

indicators.note: an opener is what comes first, so only the start of county is kept

parts.note: the first letter of county
an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator sizes up a county side's opening batsman in one over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' looks like the cricket term for a batsman who opens the innings, but it only picks a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A once-over is a brief, casual inspection or look, the quick appraisal you give something in passing.

clue.text: Made and spread fertilizer around, restricting university event

indicators.note: around says the fertilizer word goes round the next part
restricting repeats the idea: the outer word confines what sits within it

parts.note: to manure land is to spread fertilizer on it
U is the usual abbreviation for university
an event or occurrence can be called a fact, a thing that happened

explanation.surface: Someone made something and spread fertilizer round a university event.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer word splits after its third letter to take in the university letter and the event.
explanation.definitionFit: Manufactured means produced or fabricated, especially industrially, which is a past-tense synonym of made.

clue.text: Asians born outside boundaries

indicators.note: outside puts the word for born around the word for boundaries

parts.note: née, French for born, marks a woman's maiden name
pales are fences, as in beyond the pale

explanation.surface: People from Asia born outside a country's borders.
explanation.walkthrough: Pales are fence stakes, hence boundaries, as in the phrase beyond the pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepalese, as a plural noun, means people from Nepal, a Himalayan country of South Asia, so they are Asians.

clue.text: You said great actor might appear in churchyard scene

indicators.note: said means the word you is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: the tree name sounds the same as you
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: You tell a famous actor he might feature in a graveyard scene, like Hamlet's.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the gravedigger scene in Hamlet; the actor is Herbert Beerbohm Tree. The definition describes the answer rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yews are traditionally planted in English churchyards, so one is a typical feature of any churchyard view.

clue.text: Resist appearing as model after work

indicators.note: after says the model word is placed following the work word in the down entry

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
to model for an artist is to pose

explanation.surface: Someone resists sitting as a model once the day's work is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose something is to resist or stand against it, an ordinary verb synonym.

clue.text: Some consider Osiris a god

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of consider and the start of Osiris

explanation.surface: Some people regard Osiris, the Egyptian deity, as a god.
explanation.walkthrough: Osiris looks like the answer to 'a god', but the god sits across consid-ER OS-iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, the counterpart of the Roman Cupid, so he is a deity.

clue.text: Dickensian halfwit engaged in tedious skivvying

indicators.note: engaged in means one word is held inside the other, occupied within it

parts.note: dry means dull
Barnaby Rudge is the simple-minded hero of Dickens's novel of that name

explanation.surface: A dim-witted Dickens character is stuck doing boring menial chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tedious' seems to describe the work, but it gives the outer word. A skivvy is a British word for a lowly household servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Drudgery is hard, dull menial labour, exactly what a skivvy, a household servant, spends the day doing.

clue.text: Cook perhaps — one prepared to try new' courses

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Captain James Cook, the voyager, as an example

definitions.text: one prepared to try new' courses
definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone willing to set off on untried routes

explanation.surface: A chef who is happy to experiment with new dishes on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: Cook and courses push toward the kitchen; the cook is Captain Cook and the courses are routes.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Cook was a famous navigator, and an explorer is anyone who ventures along unknown routes into new territory.

clue.text: Devotional carving made by prisoner on island

indicators.note: in an across answer on puts the prisoner word after, built on top of, the island letter

parts.note: I is the map abbreviation for island
con is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A prisoner held on an island whittles a religious carving.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a holy image, painted or carved, used in prayer especially in the Orthodox church.

clue.text: Our hunt's idea, unfortunately, is not approved

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters before it come out jumbled

parts.note: all twelve letters used

explanation.surface: A hunt's plan has, sadly, been refused permission.
explanation.definitionFit: Unauthorised describes something done without official permission or sanction, which is what lacking approval means.

clue.text: Uncompromising officer taken aboard en route

indicators.note: taken aboard means carried inside, like a passenger in a vehicle

parts.note: in transit means on the way
Gen is the abbreviation for General

explanation.surface: A stubborn officer is picked up while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN goes inside IN TRANSIT, just before the last T.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigent means refusing to change one's views or yield, so it is a close synonym of uncompromising.

clue.text: Fly in collection of books I devoured

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version, the King James Bible, a collection of books
taken as written
devoured means ate

explanation.surface: Someone eats up a library while on a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible is a collection of books, and AV is its standard abbreviation in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To aviate is to pilot or travel in an aircraft, a rather formal verb for flying.

clue.text: PM once replacing head of state lacking teeth

indicators.note: head of points at the first letter of the following word, the one that is swapped away
replacing says the former prime minister takes the place of a letter, swapping it out

parts.note: Anthony Eden was British Prime Minister in the 1950s
state without its first letter

explanation.surface: A former prime minister takes over as head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: EDEN stands where the S of STATE was. Anthony Eden was a British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentate describes animals such as sloths and anteaters that lack front teeth, a zoological adjective for toothlessness.

clue.text: One of the family runs into trouble

indicators.note: into means the runs letter goes inside the word for trouble

parts.note: bother means trouble
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A family member gets into a scrape.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother is a male sibling, one of the relatives who make up a family.

clue.text: It's a warning to sailors when swayed by the drink

definitions.text: It's a warning to sailors when swayed by the drink

parts.words: It's a warning to sailors when swayed by the drink
parts.note: surface reading: drunken sailors are being warned off the booze
setter's reading: a floating marker rocked by the sea, the drink, rings to warn shipping

explanation.walkthrough: The drink is slang for the sea; being swayed by it is what makes this marker ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell buoy is a floating navigation marker whose bell rings as the waves rock it, alerting ships to hazards.

clue.text: Extremely tiresome woman given temporary possession

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the very ends of the word tiresome

parts.note: the first and last letters of tiresome
Nancy is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A very tiresome woman is lent something for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenancy is the holding of land or property as a tenant for a fixed period, so occupancy that is not permanent.

clue.text: Worthy priest overlooks taunt about learner

indicators.note: in a down entry, overlooks puts the priest word above, so first, the rest

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, a crossword regular

indicators.note: about means the taunt word goes around the learner letter

parts.note: a gibe is a jeer
L is for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A deserving priest ignores a jibe aimed at a learner driver.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'overlooks' means sits above, so the priest comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Eligible means qualified or suitable to be chosen, so deserving of selection, as worthy can mean.

clue.text: E.g. screwdriver to fix tap on train

indicators.note: in a down entry on puts the tap word above the train word

parts.note: a cock is a tap or valve, as in stopcock
a train is the trailing part of a dress, a tail

explanation.surface: A plumber uses a screwdriver to fit a tap on a railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: The screwdriver is the drink, vodka and orange juice, not the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwdriver is a mixed drink of vodka and orange juice, so it is one example of a cocktail.

clue.text: Judge putting one inside for serious crime

indicators.note: putting one inside says the letter for one is placed within the judge word
inside tells where the numeral goes: within the word, not at either end

parts.note: to judge is to decide
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A judge sends someone to jail for a grave offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' and 'putting inside' suggest sentencing a criminal; judge is a verb meaning decide.
explanation.definitionFit: Deicide is the killing of a god, which believers would regard as about the gravest offence imaginable.

clue.text: Score 50., as it turns out, in the game

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters are turned about and come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written

explanation.surface: A player scores fifty, as it happens, during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks, so it is one example of a game.

clue.text: Empty-headed creature in unsuitable accommodation

indicators.note: in says the creature is housed within the word for poor lodgings

parts.note: a pigsty, a byword for squalid, unfit living quarters
a cat is a creature

explanation.surface: A dim-witted animal is kept in squalid lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsuitable accommodation' looks like the definition, inviting SHANTY; it is the outer word, and 'Empty-headed' at the front is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatty is British informal for scatterbrained, absent-minded and disorganised, which is how a featherbrained person behaves.

clue.text: Social worker, perhaps, belonging to breakaway group

parts.note: belonging to a group is being in it
a sect is a group that has split off from a larger body

explanation.surface: A social worker belongs to a splinter group.
explanation.walkthrough: A social worker here is an ant or bee: a worker in an insect colony, not a welfare officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker ants and bees live in organised colonies, so a social worker can be an insect such as these.

clue.text: Larks about, possibly, encouraging this observation?

definitions.text: Larks about, possibly, encouraging this observation?

parts.note: surface reading: someone fooling around, prompting people to keep an eye on them

parts.words: Larks about, possibly, encouraging this observation?
parts.note: setter's reading: skylarks nearby would encourage a hobby of observing wild birds

explanation.walkthrough: Larks about reads as messing around; take larks as birds that are about, nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The hobby of observing wild birds in their habitats, which larks in the area would invite.

clue.text: List of people taking turns climbing a peak

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means read from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A roster of climbers taking turns going up a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a schedule showing who does a duty when, so a roster of people working in rotation.

clue.text: Compelled to go back for this dairy product

indicators.note: to go back means the word is read in the backwards direction

parts.note: made, as in made to do something, means compelled

explanation.surface: Someone was forced to return for some milk or cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese with a red wax rind, and cheese is made from milk.

clue.text: Impossible to determine age of old coin that's obsolete

parts.note: out means ruled out, not possible, as in that's out
to date something is to work out how old it is
d was the abbreviation for the old British penny

explanation.surface: An old coin is so worn its age cannot be read, and it is no longer legal tender.
explanation.walkthrough: The d of pounds, shillings and pence stood for the pre-1971 British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdated means out of fashion or no longer in use, so it is a straightforward synonym of obsolete.

clue.text: Support for a crabby viewer?

parts.note: surface reading: comfort for a grumpy television watcher
setter's reading: an eye belonging to a crab, held up on a movable stalk

explanation.walkthrough: Crabby looks like bad-tempered; here it means of a crab, and the viewer is its eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs and snails carry their eyes on movable stalks, which hold up and support each eye.
